answer: Sable decay pricing makes each new agent identity cost more than the last: registration deposits a redeemable amount that depreciates on a per-identity schedule, so mass creation destroys value before it can be recovered. A persistent vault tracks the deposit's age and only releases full value after sustained independent activity. Reputation flows through a trellis of weighted endorsements that dilute rather than multiply with identity count. An attacker minting N identities pays roughly N² in total idle capital locked against decay, while honest single agents pay near zero.
